title: The Day the Sky Blew Up
narration: thirty June nineteen oh eight. A fireball streaks over Siberia, then silence. No crater. Just flattened trees over an area of approximately two thousand square kilometers. A fireball. A blast. A mystery that would outlast empires.
visual_goal: Aerial shot of dense Siberian forest, then a sudden bright flash from the sky. The forest flattens in a wave. Cut to black.

title: The Blast That Circles the World
narration: The shockwave screamed across one thousand kilometers of taiga. It circled the Earth twice before the last ripple faded. Energy? ten megatons, one hundred eighty-five Hiroshimas, detonated in an instant.
visual_goal: Global map with concentric circles expanding from Siberia. A red pulse radiates outward, looping twice around the planet.

title: Vanavara: 65 Kilometers of Lucky Survivors
narration: Sixty-five kilometers away, Vanavara’s trading post became a furnace. Windows exploded like gunshots. Men and women were hurled to the ground as the air itself turned to fire. Yet no one died.
visual_goal: Black-and-white photo of Vanavara post-explosion: shattered windows, debris. A man stumbles, looking up in shock.

title: The Night the Sky Glowed
narration: For several days, Europe and Asia woke to a sky so bright it erased the stars. You could trace the veins in your hands by its glow. Then, gone.
visual_goal: Time-lapse of a night sky over a European city. Stars fade into a luminous twilight, then return to darkness.
search_queries: Tunguska event two days bright sky

title: The Mystery That Remains
narration: No crater. No fragments. Just an airburst at an estimated altitude. The sky exploded, and left no trace. No crater. No fragments. Just a sky that burned too bright, and vanished without a trace.
visual_goal: Aerial shot of the Tunguska site today: dense forest, no visible scar. A single tree stands bent at the top, like a witness.
